title.narrative: World Bank Trust Fund Cash Transfers

description.narrative:
Stöd under 2019-2022 med totalt 75 miljoner SEK till utbyggnad av nationella sociala kontantstöd via Världsbankens Multi Donor Trust Fund, med fokus på att registrera fler förmånstagare, öka bidragsbeloppen (socialbidrag, barnbidrag, beredskapsarbete m.m.) samt stärka kapaciteten på socialförsäkringsmyndigheten INAS. Total budget för programmet är ca 180 miljoner SEK och andra givare är Storbritannien och Nederländerna. Det svenska bidraget uppgår till ca 41 procent an total budget. Fonden är aktiv sedan slutet av 2018.
Insatsen förväntas bidra till effektiva och transparenta utbetalningar samt till att vidareutveckla registret över förmånstagare (e-INAS ). Stödet är ett av de insatser i den svenska portföljen som tydligt kommer att svara mot de effekter som cyklonen IDAI medfört i de centrala delarna av landet. Minst 18 500 hushåll kommer att nås av insatsen, en siffra som kan komma att öka dramatiskt då fler givare kommer in med särskilt stöd till cyklondrabbade områden.

Support during 2019-2022 with a total sum of 75 million SEK to scale-up the national social cash transfer system through a World Bank Multi Donor Trust Fund. Total budget is ca 180 million SEK, and other donors are UK and the Netherlands. Swedish share around 41 percent of total budget. The fund is active since end of 2018.
Focus is on scaling up cash transfers (social cash transfers, child grant, public works salaries) and on increasing the number of beneficiaries. The contribution is expected to strengthen INAS, the agency for social security, assure an efficient and transparent payment system and develop the beneficary registry (e-INAS). The support is one of the contributions that will reply to the negative effects of the cyclone IDAI in the central parts of the country.
At least 18 500 households will be reached by the intervention, a number toat may increase dramatically as more donors are coming in with specific support to mitigate for the effects of the cyclones.

The Multi-Donor Trust Fund Strengthening Mozambiques Social Protection System (MozSP MDTF) supports the scale up of Social protection coverage and strengthen delivery systems through a pooled funding approach for donor partner engagement in the SP sector in Mozambique.
The development objective of the MozSP is to strengthen the social protection system in Mozambique and it is designed to:
(i) increased coverage of poor households; (ii) generate knowledge and evidence-based instruments that improve efficiency of existing SP systems; and (iii) enhanced coordination with development partners.
The MozSP finances grants which contribute to the achievement of these objectives, these are structured in two pillars: Recipient-Executed activities (RETF): implemented by the Government of Mozambique (GoM) through Ministry of Labour, Gender and Social Action (MTGAS) and National Institute of Social Action (INAS).These activities are designed to strengthen coverage of existing social protection programs, prioritize income support to eligible households in existing Social Protection programs by financing existing income support cash transfers, associated implementation costs, and piloting and scaling up solutions that enhance the efficiency and impact of SP programs.
Bank-Executed activities (BETF): implemented by WB, including through local and international individual consultants as well as firms. These activities finance the provision of technical assistance to contribute to the knowledge generation, development and testing of innovative solutions to improve the functioning of SP systems in the following areas (i) strengthening the delivery systems of existing social programs, (ii) enhancing intersectoral synergies; and (iii) improving coordination and integration of the SP system. The BETF activities are designed to complement and support the implementation of the WB SPER project and other WB projects1 in the Human Development sector

title.narrative: Agreement amendment Strengthening Mozambique Social Protection System

description.narrative:
Recipient executed activities
Strengthening Social Protection Delivery Systems - - Digital Payments Expansion: significant progress was made in transitioning social protection payments to digital methods. Contracts with three main service providers (M-PESA, EMOLA, MKESH) were signed, enabling the opening of 136,000 digital accounts and successful digital payments to over 20,000 beneficiaries. This shift reduced costs and improved efficiency. - eINAS System Improvements: enhancements to the Management Information System (eINAS) included fixing bugs, adding new functionalities for beneficiary enrollment, and integrating new electronic payment providers. These improvements streamlined workflows and supported program management. - Proxy Means Test (PMT) Review: analytical work began to improve the accuracy and trust in the PMT model, which is central to targeting social protection programs. Results are expected in the next reporting.
Improving Effectiveness and Efficiency of Social Protection Programs - PASP Public Works: the program reached 71,451 households in 58 districts in the provinces of Cabo Delegado, Nampula, Niassa and Zambézia, with 92% compliance in payments. Efforts to expand coverage to 36 additional districts are underway. - PASP-ADIGR: Kits were distributed to 16,978 beneficiaries (69% female), with plans to reach 48,358 beneficiaries in total.
Shock-Responsive Social Protection - PASD-PE Payments: payments were completed for 150,000 emergency response beneficiaries, with 54,000 payments made digitally and most through the semi-digital OPA system (96,000). Efforts are ongoing to resolve issues for 41,000 residual beneficiaries who have not received the benefit for some reason, for example: blocking of the M-pesa account or absences.
Bank executed
Strengthening SP delivery systems: The Bank executed activities related to systems delivery have contributed to key outcomes in the sector, particularly the digital payments agenda. In 2024 the GoM made a policy decision to roll out digital payments in the social protection sector and investments in this area are having an impact. The technical assistance and analytical work supported by the Bank is now providing key evidence on how to best to achieve this MEF endorsed decision. Recommendations from the multi study on Lessons from payment mechanisms implemented by INAS, as well as the previously developed Digital Readiness Score are presented in key debates and discussions among GoM and development partners and the Bank is leading the agenda on digital payment solutions.
The studies on the digital social protection payment solutions have concluded that there are important opportunities to expand digital payments, especially in urbanized areas. Like in many countries, more work is needed to make the current G2P digital payments environment more conducive. The main challenges are regulatory financial and legal restrictions for account opening; limited formal financial access points; low connectivity; and low coverage of the population registry. Also, continued engagement with the private sector is critical to ensure purposeful increase of coverage of agents and infrastructure, as well as improvement of quality and suitable service to vulnerable population.
The technical assistance on eINAS is also a major achievement for this reporting period. Despite many attempts, previous discussions between development partners and the GoM had failed to find a way forward and systems improvements had been paused due to institutional issues and this was hampering the overall functionality of the system. In the first semester of 2024 a common agenda was agreed between INAS and CEDSIF and the software work since May has been paving the way for larger systems improvement and ultimately to have all modules within the eINAS fully functioning.
Coordination Mechanisms The MDTF supported an assignment to improve the coordination and dialogue in the SP sector with partners and government, which started in 2022. In June 2024 a revised coordination structure for SP partners structure was proposed but consensus was not reached on the need to have a donor only working group. The MDTF also supports coordination via financing of the SP Secretariat. A roadmap for improved dialogue and coordination was developed, including the ONE VOICE agenda and ONE PLAN dashboard linked to the National Basic Social Security Strategy (ENSSB II). These tools aim to harmonize partner activities and funding by: - strengthening and streamline the development partners (DPs) internal dialogue and coordination mechanisms to more effectively engage with the SP sector. - reducing the transactions costs for both Government and DPs of dealing with multiple DPs by synthesizing key issues to engage government with One Voice. - supporting the government in the development and implementation of national social protection priorities as defined in the ENSSB II and possibly III and its specific operational plans.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
